<objective>
Close the agent-capability slice: a task, a repository, or Fleet's own config can each name a profile with
the same precedence the phase already uses for caps and models; a repository can only ever NAME one; and
every way a profile can be wrong fails the spawn loudly instead of producing a session that quietly lacks
its capability.

Purpose: plan `02-11` proved one profile reaches one spawn. This plan makes the profile CHOOSABLE at the
three levels AGENT-05 names, makes the repository-side channel a string and nothing more, and makes every
failure mode visible. The failure half matters most: the whole class of bug this requirement exists to
prevent is a run that succeeds while missing the tools it was supposed to have — indistinguishable from a
working run until someone notices the work did not happen.

Output: a `.fleet.yml` with exactly one new key, a nullable `tasks.agent_profile` column with its
migration, a shared precedence table proving the three resolvers agree, four distinct fail-loud paths, and
a blocking human gate for the one clause no hermetic test can reach.
</objective>

  <action>
Make the profile choosable at three levels with one precedence implementation.

**`src/registry/fleet-yaml.ts`** — add exactly one key to `fleetYmlSchema`: an optional string named for the
agent profile, mirroring the existing `env_profile` entry both in type and in intent. A repository NAMES a
profile; it never defines one. Extend the module header comment to say so explicitly, in the same voice as
the existing sentence about `setup`/`test` being read and displayed only, because that comment is the
durable record a future reader will find first.

Then reverse plan `02-08`'s per-project allowed-tools override if it landed: if `fleetYmlSchema` carries an
`allowed_tools` key, remove it and every consumer that reads it, and route the same intent through the
profile's extra allowed tools instead. D-36 subsumes D-10's promise deliberately — two routes to widen a
tool list means two places to audit and two places for them to disagree. Leave any `disallowed_tools` key
alone: that one only ever tightens, so it carries no capability-granting surface and no boundary argument
applies to it. If `02-08` did not add `allowed_tools`, note that in the summary and change nothing.

**`src/db/schema.ts`** — add a nullable text column to `tasks` for the agent profile name, immediately
after the `model` column so the three inheritable settings sit together. Nullable means inherit, exactly as
`max_turns` and `wall_clock_cap_ms` already do — do not introduce a sentinel string, and do not give the
column a default.

**The migration** — run `npm run db:generate -- --name agent_profile` so drizzle-kit emits
`drizzle/0001_agent_profile.sql` and updates `drizzle/meta/_journal.json` and the snapshot. Do not
hand-write the SQL: `runMigrations` applies the trail through drizzle's journal, and a file whose hash is
absent from the journal is silently skipped, producing a database that passes every test and lacks the
column. Confirm the generated statement adds the column rather than rebuilding the table, and confirm the
existing packaging test still passes — `build:assets` copies the whole migrations directory, so a second
migration needs no packaging change, only proof that it ships.

**`src/runner/agent-profile.ts`** — export `resolveAgentProfileName(input)`, a PURE function taking the
three candidate values in the order AGENT-05 names — task, repository, Fleet config — and returning the
first non-null, or null when all are absent. Give it the same input-object shape `resolveModel` uses so a
single shared precedence table can exercise both. Do not read the config file inside it; the caller supplies
all three values, which is what makes it testable without a filesystem and what lets the shared table
compare it against the other two resolvers directly.

**`src/tasks/service.ts`** — accept an optional agent profile name on `CreateTaskInput` and write it into
the INSERT. Resolve nothing here beyond the task level: the repository and Fleet-config levels are read at
dispatch time, not at creation time, because `.fleet.yml` is read live and never snapshotted (Phase 1 D-17)
— snapshotting the repository's choice at creation would make a task ignore a `.fleet.yml` edit that landed
before it was dispatched, which is precisely the staleness D-17 exists to prevent.

**`src/scheduler/queue.ts`** — in `dispatch()`, replace plan `02-11`'s single default wire with the full
order: read the task row's profile column, call `readFleetYml(project.repoPath)` and take its config's
profile key (the same live read WT-05's setup commands already perform — do not add a second read if one
is already in the dispatch path, reuse its result), read Fleet's configured default, and pass all three
through `resolveAgentProfileName`. Assign the result to `RunnerTask.agentProfileName`. A `.fleet.yml` that
fails to parse yields a null config and a warning; treat that as "the repository named nothing" and fall
through to the Fleet default rather than failing the task — an unparseable optional file is a warning
condition the registry already models, not a dispatch failure.

**`src/api/http/routes/tasks.ts`** — add an optional agent-profile-name string to `createTaskBody`. It is a
NAME, so constrain it the way a name is constrained: non-empty, and matching a conservative identifier
pattern with no path separator and no leading dot, so it cannot be mistaken for or coerced into a path.
The body still accepts no path component of any kind.

**`src/api/http/errors.ts`** — add the four profile error codes to `CODE_TO_STATUS`: profile-not-found and
config-directory-missing as 404, invalid-profile and unknown-MCP-server as 422. No new `instanceof` branch
is needed — plan `02-04` added a generic branch that renders any thrown `Error` whose `code` is a key of
this map, and membership in the map is the allowlist.

**`src/cli/index.ts`** — add an `--agent-profile <name>` option to `task create`, passed straight through
in the request body, and add a column for it to `taskColumns` so `fleet task show` reveals which profile a
task ran under. A task whose profile is inherited rather than task-level should render distinguishably from
one with no profile at all — an em dash for inherited-and-unresolved is not the same as showing a resolved
name, and conflating them hides the exact thing this requirement is about. Preserve the CLI-isolation
constraint: declare any wire shape locally, import nothing from `../db/` or `../registry/`.
  </action>
